operational_flag.verdict: COVERAGE FIXED, ONE RECURRING NIGHTLY BLACKOUT
operational_flag.coverage_24h: 79 state-file commits in the last 24h against ~72 expected (110%), up from 31% on 07-26. The 5h45m self-looping job plus the 7,27,47 cron shift solved the daytime starvation problem.
operational_flag.pattern: This is the SECOND consecutive night with an almost identical gap - 367 min on 07-28 21:40Z -> 07-29 03:47Z. A blackout that repeats to within one minute of duration in the same ~22:00Z-04:00Z window is systematic, not random throttling. Mechanism: bot.yml uses concurrency with cancel-in-progress:false, so a running 5h45m loop holds the lock and the successor run sits queued; overnight the successor is not started for ~6h. Run 30487805365 (created 07-29 20:16Z) shows updatedAt 07-30 04:04Z with no data commits in between, and 30500605056 (created 07-29 23:46Z) only began at 04:04Z.
operational_flag.failed_runs: 0 failures. 11 consecutive bot.yml runs since 07-26 21:05Z conclude 'cancelled', which is consistent with the 355-minute timeout-minutes cap firing at the end of the 345-minute internal loop (GitHub labels a timed-out job 'cancelled'). INFERRED, not confirmed - the runs do commit their full cycle output first.
operational_flag.recommendation: The owner's pre-agreed escalation to an external trigger is now warranted, scoped to the 22:00Z-04:00Z handoff window specifically rather than the whole schedule.
operational_flag.gh_run_list_caveat: gh run list WITHOUT --workflow bot.yml is dominated by pages-build-deployment runs fired by each data commit and will read as healthy 13-minute cadence even during a blackout. Gaps must be computed from data/ commit timestamps.
